sentences.text: Dryornis, meaning "tree bird" and also known as the Argentinian vulture, is an extinct genus of New World vulture from the early Miocene to early Pliocene of Argentina.
This animal stands as the largest known cathartiform bird, excluding the Teratornithidae family.
It is distinguished by a highly pneumatized sternum, likely an adaptation for its large size and flight.
Analysis of fossils suggests Dryornis had a body mass of 26 kg.
The wingspan of Dryornis pampeanus was likely between 3.87 and 4 meters.
The genus Dryornis was first described in 1891 by Argentine paleontologists Francisco Moreno and Alcides Mercerat.
The type species Dryornis pampeanus was originally based on a right humerus and a right femur.
The species Dryornis hatcheri was described in 2022 by Federico J. Degrange after it remained unstudied since its initial discovery.
The original fossils of Dryornis were collected from the Pliocene-age Monte Hermoso Formation in Buenos Aires, Argentina.
Fossils from the La Estafeta Beach in Mar del Plata allowed detailed phylogenetic analysis and revealed new diagnostic characteristics for Dryornis pampeanus.
Phylogenetic analyses place Dryornis within the family Cathartidae as a sister taxon to Coragyps and Cathartes.
Dryornis lived from the Aquitanian to the Zanclean stages, approximately 23.04 to 3.8 million years ago.
